[Tour Detail] Integrate Upload Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN uploads finished tours to GoThru via /streeteditor/upload-tour (apil.gothru.co); see docs/analyze.md §2.7, §3.4, and the upload-reliability notes in §5.

Goal

Implement "Upload Tour" in the Flutter app: send a local tour (project + panoramas + connections + levels) to GoThru, with progress, pre-checks, and clear success/failure handling.

Scope

  • Pre-upload checks: connectivity, storage/quota, per-panorama GoThru existence (skip already-present panoramas).
  • Upload project metadata, panorama assets, connections, and levels.
  • Progress feedback (per-panorama / overall); update local uploaded / virtual_tour_status.
  • Surface errors with retry; no silent failure.

Out of Scope

  • Retry-condition fix specifics (tracked in the RN repo); moderation; Google publishing.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Upload sends the full tour and reflects true server state on completion (uploaded/virtual_tour_status).
  • Pre-checks (network, storage, per-panorama existence) run before/within upload.
  • Progress shown; already-uploaded panoramas are skipped (no duplicates).
  • Errors surfaced with retry; partial uploads are resumable/clean.
  • Works with the signed-in session token.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Upload a tour (happy path)

  1. Open a complete local tour → Upload.
  2. Expected: Upload completes; tour marked uploaded; appears correctly on GoThru.

TC-2 — Skip already-uploaded panoramas

  1. Upload a tour where some panoramas already exist on GoThru.
  2. Expected: Only missing panoramas are sent; no duplicates server-side.

TC-3 — Offline / no connection

  1. Attempt upload offline.
  2. Expected: Clear "no internet" message; upload not started.

TC-4 — Quota / storage exceeded

  1. Upload when over quota.
  2. Expected: Clear error; no broken partial state looping.

TC-5 — Interruption + retry

  1. Interrupt mid-upload, then retry.
  2. Expected: Resumes remaining work; completes; one tour, no duplicates.

TC-6 — Progress feedback

  1. Upload a large tour.
  2. Expected: Visible progress; UI not frozen.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: local tour data intact whether upload succeeds or fails.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED — real-data mobile validation found an upload-blocking coding defect. The upload did not complete; unexecuted scenarios are not marked as passed.

ID Method Scenario Result Status
TC-1 Gray Box Upload a complete local tour Upload failed during the prepare connections stage with HTTP 409: level already exist FAIL — Bug
TC-2 Gray Box Skip already-uploaded panoramas Not executed because the upload was blocked before completion Not executed
TC-3 Black Box Attempt upload while offline Not executed in this run Not executed
TC-4 Black Box Upload while quota or storage is exceeded Not executed; no safe quota-exceeded QA condition was used Not executed
TC-5 Gray / Black Box Interrupt an upload and retry Not executed because the initial upload was blocked Not executed
TC-6 White / Gray Box Verify progress on a large upload The upload reached preparation but could not proceed past the failing connection preparation step Blocked by bug
Regression Gray Box Verify local tour data after failed upload Requires final device confirmation after the failed attempt; not asserted as passed in this run Not executed

Confirmed Coding Bug

Severity Actual result Expected result Impact
High Upload Tour fails at prepare connections with HTTP 409 level already exist. The upload must prepare and upload the tour's connections and levels without rejecting a valid existing level, or it must handle an already-existing level idempotently. A tour containing the affected level/connection state cannot be uploaded to GoThru.

Remaining upload behavior Not evaluated after the blocking failure Not executed

Server conflict is visible to the user The failure message was shown Pass

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED. The original upload blocker is fixed, but the completed upload does not preserve the local panorama-to-level mapping.

Retest Result

New Confirmed Coding Bug — Panorama Level Mapping Is Not Preserved

Severity Steps Expected result Actual result Impact
High Create a local six-panorama tour; create Levels 2 and 3; assign two panoramas to each level; upload; wait for completion; reload the uploaded GoThru Listing. Exactly six panoramas remain distributed as local: Level 1 = 2, Level 2 = 2, Level 3 = 2. The uploaded listing displays Level 1 = 4, Level 2 = 2, Level 3 = 2: eight panoramas total. Upload completes but produces an incorrect server-side tour structure, with two unexpected panoramas in Level 1.

Evidence

  • Real-device mobile recording reviewed: [TourDetail]IntegrateUploadTour#35.mp4 (3:37).
  • The recording shows six local panoramas before upload, the Upload Complete dialog, then the reloaded GoThru Listing with level counters 1 = 4, 2 = 2, and 3 = 2.

Evidence type: tester-supplied real-device mobile validation. The recording is retained locally and was not uploaded to GitHub in this update.

[Fullscreen] Integrate Device Motion (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN uses gyro-driven viewing via expo-sensors + custom DeviceOrientationControls (src/threejs); see docs/analyze.md §3.1. Flutter port uses device sensors (gyroscope/accelerometer) to drive the panorama camera.

Goal

Implement device-motion control in the fullscreen panorama viewer: moving/rotating the phone pans the 360° view (gyro-driven look-around), with a toggle.

Scope

  • Use device orientation sensors to drive yaw/pitch in the fullscreen viewer.
  • A toggle to enable/disable motion control (fallback to drag).
  • Smooth, low-latency response; sensible calibration to current heading.

Out of Scope

  • Base panorama rendering (separate task), zoom, arrows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Enabling device motion makes the view follow phone movement.
  • Toggle switches between motion and drag control cleanly.
  • Motion is smooth (no excessive jitter/lag).
  • Disabling restores drag-only control.
  • Handles devices lacking the required sensors gracefully.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Motion control (happy path)

  1. Open fullscreen → enable Device Motion → move the phone.
  2. Expected: The view pans following the phone's orientation.

TC-2 — Toggle off

  1. Disable Device Motion.
  2. Expected: View stops following motion; drag still works.

TC-3 — Smoothness

  1. Rotate the phone steadily.
  2. Expected: Smooth tracking; no severe jitter or drift.

TC-4 — Calibration

  1. Enable motion at a given heading.
  2. Expected: View aligns sensibly with the current orientation (no jarring jump).

TC-5 — No sensors

  1. Run on a device without gyroscope (or simulate).
  2. Expected: Graceful fallback to drag; clear handling, no crash.

TC-6 — Background/return

  1. Background the app during motion, then return.
  2. Expected: Motion resumes correctly; no stuck state.

Platforms: Android + iOS (physical device needed for sensors)
Regression watch: drag control and rendering unaffected when motion is off.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED — real-device mobile validation with real data found one device-motion coding defect. All other executed task scenarios passed.

ID Method Scenario Real-device result Status
TC-1 White / Gray Box Enable Device Motion and rotate the phone Motion mode enabled and the panorama responded to device movement PASS
TC-2 Gray Box Disable Device Motion and use drag control Motion stopped and drag control continued to work PASS
TC-3 Black Box Rotate the phone steadily General motion response remained usable; see the confirmed vertical-orientation defect below FAIL — Bug
TC-4 Gray Box Enable motion from a chosen panorama heading Motion mode enabled without a disruptive initial jump PASS
TC-5 Black Box Sensor-unavailable fallback The fallback was handled safely with no application crash PASS
TC-6 Black Box Background the application during motion and return Motion resumed correctly with no stuck state or crash PASS
Regression Gray / Black Box Use fullscreen viewer with motion disabled Panorama rendering and drag interaction remained unaffected; no panorama or tour data changed PASS

Confirmed Coding Bug

Severity Actual result Expected result Impact
High After rotating the phone from down to up through one full movement and returning it to the forward-facing position, the point of view did not return to the panorama front. The bottom of the panorama was displayed instead. The point of view must track the phone orientation consistently and return near the front view when the phone returns to its original forward-facing orientation. Vertical device-motion navigation is inaccurate and disorienting; users cannot reliably look around the panorama with phone motion.

Code Review Summary

Area Reviewed behavior Result
Motion toggle The fullscreen viewer provides separate motion and gesture modes PASS
Gesture fallback Disabling motion restores drag-based navigation PASS
Sensor lifecycle Motion pauses in the background and resumes when the app returns PASS
Orientation integration Vertical orientation does not return to the expected view after the tested rotation FAIL — Bug
Data safety Fullscreen viewing and motion mode do not modify panorama or tour data PASS

Background and return Motion resumed without a stuck state Pass
Panorama and tour data integrity No data change was observed Pass

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED. The current Device Motion fix did not resolve the vertical-orientation defect on a physical mobile device.

Check Expected Actual Status
Device Motion toggle Motion control can be enabled in the fullscreen viewer Enabled during the retest Pass
Vertical return-to-origin After moving the phone down/up and returning it to its original forward-facing position, the POV returns near the original front view The POV drifts to the panorama bottom and does not return consistently to the starting view Fail — Bug

Confirmed Coding Bug — Vertical Device Motion Drift

Severity Steps Expected result Actual result Impact
High Open a fullscreen panorama; enable Device Motion; move the phone through the vertical down/up movement; return it to its original forward-facing position. The viewpoint should return near the initial front-facing panorama orientation. The viewpoint drifts to the panorama bottom instead of returning consistently to the initial view. Vertical gyro navigation remains inaccurate and disorienting.

Evidence

  • Tester-supplied real-device recording, 2:05: [Fullscreen]IntegrateDeviceMotion#43.mp4.
  • The recording shows Device Motion enabled and the panorama ending at the lower portion rather than reliably returning to its starting orientation.

Evidence type: real-device mobile sanity test. The result is a confirmed product defect, not a test-environment limitation.

[Listing Detail] Discard Changes (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: Listing detail lets the user abandon unsaved local edits and revert to the last saved/server state (see docs/analyze.md §2.6, §3.3 projects/panoramas).

Goal

Implement "Discard Changes" in Listing Detail: revert any unsaved local edits to the listing back to the last saved/server state, with confirmation.

Scope

  • Discard action (with confirm) that drops pending local edits to the listing.
  • Restore fields/assets to the last saved/server values.
  • Reflect the reverted state in the UI immediately.

Out of Scope

  • Saving/updating (separate task); deleting the listing/tour.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Discard prompts for confirmation before reverting.
  • On confirm, unsaved edits are dropped and the last saved/server state is restored.
  • Cancel keeps the in-progress edits.
  • UI reflects the reverted state immediately; no partial/garbled state.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Discard edits (happy path)

  1. Open a listing → make edits → Discard Changes → confirm.
  2. Expected: Edits removed; listing shows the last saved/server values.

TC-2 — Cancel discard

  1. Make edits → Discard → cancel.
  2. Expected: Edits are kept; nothing reverted.

TC-3 — No edits

  1. Tap Discard with no pending changes.
  2. Expected: Graceful no-op / informs nothing to discard.

TC-4 — Discard then re-edit

  1. Discard, then make new edits.
  2. Expected: Editing works normally after a discard.

TC-5 — Navigation guard (if applicable)

  1. Try to leave the screen with unsaved edits.
  2. Expected: Prompt to discard/keep, per the defined behavior.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Confirmation/labels translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: discard reverts only the current listing's unsaved edits — no server data is changed.

QA Summary — 5 August 2026

QA status: Needs developer confirmation

Manual validation was completed on a real mobile device using real data. The expected Discard Changes popup did not appear after the tested edits. This is recorded as a QA note pending developer confirmation; it is not yet classified as a coding bug.

Result and scope clarification

The current Listing Detail behavior saves supported edits directly to GoThru/web:

  • Adding a level is integrated with GoThru and saves immediately.
  • Moving a panorama to another level is integrated with GoThru and saves immediately.
  • Connection editing could not be used as a pending-local-change scenario during this validation.

Therefore, there is no available user action that leaves an unsaved local edit and triggers the Discard Changes confirmation. The absence of the dialog in this flow is expected because the validated changes have already been saved to GoThru. This may be an intended scope/behavior difference from the original issue description. Developer confirmation is required before classifying it as a coding bug.

TC-2 Gray box Move a panorama to another level, then navigate back Move saved directly to GoThru; no unsaved state or discard dialog PASS
TC-3 Black box Attempt to find an available unsaved-edit action No eligible pending-local-change action found; connection edit was not available for this test Not executable under current behavior
TC-4 Gray box Confirm changes are retained after navigating back Saved level/panorama-level changes remained integrated with GoThru/web PASS
TC-5 Gray box Back navigation after supported edits No discard prompt, because the edits were already saved PASS
TC-6 White box Discard labels/dialog localization Not executable: dialog has no reachable unsaved-change state in the validated flow Not executable under current behavior

QA note for developer: The Discard Changes popup did not appear after adding a level or moving a panorama. These actions were already integrated and saved to GoThru/web. Please confirm whether no reachable unsaved-change state is the intended behavior for this task. Bug classification: Pending confirmation.
